**This is a pre-release for testing.** It is not marked Latest and is not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use [v0.5.0](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.5.0).

This is the fourth beta of 0.5.1. Since beta.3: **distant scenery keeps its light**, because mipmap levels are now averaged in linear light. **The GPU encoder is about twice as fast** and gives way to the tiles X-Plane is waiting for, and if the GPU fails mid-flight, encoding falls back to the CPU. **Night lighting is generated in about half the time, and its textures stay in memory through a scene load.** An error XEarthLayer recovers from no longer takes the scenery away. If you tested beta.3, see "Coming from an earlier 0.5.1 beta" below.

0.5.1's biggest change is on macOS: **XEarthLayer no longer uses macFUSE's kernel extension.** It mounts its scenery through macFUSE's FSKit backend instead, so a new Mac no longer has to boot into Recovery and lower its security. On every platform, night lighting draws **street lamps along real roads**, cities are lit closer to what you see from the air, and **`network.connections`** keeps XEarthLayer from overwhelming home routers.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.4-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS 15.4 or newer, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.4-arm64-macos.pkg`, Homebrew (below), or `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.4-arm64-macos.tar.gz` |

No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews. There is no Intel Mac build; Intel Mac users can build from source. The `xearthlayer-publish` downloads are the package publishing tool, which testers do not need.

XEarthLayer is now licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. Releases up to beta.2 remain available under MIT. Nothing changes in how it works.

## Setup

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer before you start.

### 1. macOS only: set up macFUSE for FSKit

This build needs **macOS 15.4 or later** and **macFUSE 5.3.3 or later**. [docs/macos.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.1/docs/macos.md) walks through each step.

1. Install or update [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io). If you already have 5.3.3 or later, keep it.
2. Open **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions**, click the ⓘ next to **File System Extensions**, and turn on **macFUSE (local)**. System Settings may list both **macFUSE** and **macFUSE (local)**; XEarthLayer needs **macFUSE (local)**.
3. If X-Plane is on an **external drive** (under `/Volumes`):
   - Give `/usr/libexec/fskitd` Full Disk Access under **Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access** (click **+**, press `Cmd+Shift+G` and type the path).
   - The drive must have ownership turned on. XEarthLayer checks this when it starts, and if ownership is off it stops and prints the `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` command for your drive.

Coming from 0.5.0? You no longer need the kernel extension you approved for it. Steps 1 and 2 are still needed: the kernel extension approval does not turn on the file system extension.

### 2. Install the binary

**Linux:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.4-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.4
```

**macOS**, choose **one** of the three ways below.

**With the installer package.** Download `xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.4-arm64-macos.pkg`, double-click it and follow the Installer. It puts `xearthlayer` in `/usr/local/bin`, which is already on your `PATH`. The package is signed and notarized with the ticket attached, so it installs without a network connection. In a new terminal:

```bash
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.4
```

**With Homebrew.** The pre-release channel follows every alpha, beta and rc build:

```bash
brew install --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.4
```

If macFUSE is already installed from its own installer, add `--skip-cask-deps`. Already on the channel? `brew upgrade --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease` is all you need.

**From the tarball.** Safari unpacks the download into a folder for you (`cd ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.4-arm64-macos`); with any other browser, `cd ~/Downloads` and `tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.1-beta.4-arm64-macos.tar.gz`. Then:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.1-beta.4
```

If `xearthlayer --version` prints something else, an older copy comes first on your `PATH`: `which -a xearthlayer` lists every copy.

### Coming from an earlier 0.5.1 beta?

Install the binary (step 2).

- **From beta.3**, there is nothing else to do: no setting was added or removed.
- **From beta.1 or beta.2**, bring the configuration up to date:

  ```bash
  xearthlayer config upgrade
  ```

  It removes `texture.format`, which no longer exists: XEarthLayer encodes BC1 only, and choosing BC3 never produced usable scenery. A configuration that still has the line loads as before.

Then read "After upgrading" below and go to step 5.

### 3. Coming from 0.5.0 or a 0.5.0 preview?

Your configuration and packages carry over. Bring the configuration up to date:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

It adds the new `[network]` section and removes `fuse.macos_backend` and `texture.format`, which no longer exist. Then read "After upgrading" below and go to step 5.

**One default changes for everyone:** `network.connections` is `high`, so XEarthLayer now opens a fifth fewer connections than 0.5.0 did. If you have prosumer or enterprise network hardware and want 0.5.0's limits back, `xearthlayer config set network.connections max`.

### 4. New to XEarthLayer, or coming from v0.4.8?

Run `xearthlayer setup`. It asks for the network connections level as step 4: **High** suits most home routers, **Max** needs prosumer or enterprise network hardware, and **Low** is for older or low spec routers. When it finishes it offers to open the package manager, where you install the regions you fly (press `2` for the Library, mark regions with `Space`, press `i`).

Coming from v0.4.8, follow the upgrade steps in the [v0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.5.0) first: the rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the old packages must be removed before new ones are installed.

### After upgrading

- **Tiles already in the cache keep their darker distant levels** until the cache replaces them, so for a while a new tile beside an old one may look lighter at long range. The difference is larger than beta.3's fix: up to an eighth of the light, more on some tiles. To see the change everywhere at once, run `xearthlayer cache clear`, which deletes only the cache. The first flight afterwards builds every tile again from imagery already downloaded.
- **Night lighting now shares `cache.memory_size`.** With a memory cache above about 1.7 GB, night lighting takes 15% of it and scenery tiles keep 85%; with 8 GB, that is about 1.3 GB for night lighting. Below about 1.7 GB, night lighting keeps its 256 MB on top of the memory cache, as before.
- Night lighting saved on disk by an earlier 0.5.1 beta stays valid.

From beta.1, beta.2 or 0.5.0, also:

- **Settings are checked when XEarthLayer starts.** A value in `config.ini` outside its range, for example from editing the file by hand, now stops XEarthLayer with a message naming the setting and its range, instead of being used as written. Correct it as the message says. `prefetch.box_extent = 6.5`, an old default, is read as 7.0, and `config upgrade` rewrites it.
- **The first start downloads some imagery again.** Downloaded imagery is now kept per imagery provider, and the old shared imagery cache is deleted in the background the first time XEarthLayer starts. Tiles already built stay in the cache; only a tile that has to be built again downloads its imagery again.

### 5. Run

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

---

## What changed since beta.3

**Scenery tiles**

- **Distant scenery keeps its light.** Each smaller version of a texture, which X-Plane draws in the distance, was averaged from the stored pixel values, which are not proportional to light, so each one came out darker than the one above it. On 40 tiles of the San Francisco Bay Area, an eighth of the light was gone by the eighth level, and up to a quarter on some tiles. Levels are now averaged in light, and keep the light of the tile to within 0.3%, with the CPU and GPU encoders alike. Distant towns, hills and coasts look lighter and more detailed; forest, fields and water look as before. Building a tile takes about 7% more CPU time.
- **An error XEarthLayer recovers from no longer takes the scenery away.** Any panic, even one caught inside a single tile's work, unmounted the scenery, leaving the dashboard up but X-Plane with an empty scenery folder until XEarthLayer was restarted. The scenery now stays mounted until XEarthLayer really exits.
- **A failure while starting under the dashboard no longer hangs** with the loading screen up and the scenery mounted. It ends `run`, which unmounts.

**GPU encoder** (`texture.compressor = gpu`)

- **About twice as fast.** The GPU builds each tile's smaller levels itself, takes the whole tile in one step instead of thirteen, and starts the next tile while one finishes. On the laptop it was measured on, a tile X-Plane is waiting for is ready in about 9 ms instead of 17.
- **Tiles X-Plane is waiting for go first.** They no longer queue behind prefetch tiles; one waits at most for the prefetch tile already on the GPU.
- **A GPU that fails mid-flight no longer stops scenery from loading.** After a lost, hung or crashed GPU, or three slow tiles in a row, XEarthLayer encodes on the CPU (ISPC) for the rest of the session, and the Status pane says `GPU failed, encoding on CPU (ISPC)` with the reason. A tile that has waited more than 2 seconds for the GPU is encoded on the CPU straight away.
- **The flight log reports where the GPU's time goes**: a `GPU encode sample` line every minute, with the GPU's own compute time where the driver supports timestamps.

**Night lighting**

- **Generated in about half the time**, and encoded in half the time with a sixth of the memory. The textures are byte for byte the same.
- **Night textures stay in memory through a scene load.** The memory cache keeps a texture's small levels apart from its largest one, which most textures never need, and its size follows `cache.memory_size` (see "After upgrading").
- **Night textures are ready sooner when scenery loads.** One is generated as soon as XEarthLayer tells X-Plane it has light, before X-Plane reads it; the textures X-Plane is reading go first, and early generation pauses while X-Plane waits for a scenery tile.
- **Areas lit only by roads no longer stay dark** when reading the roads is slow, and a city lit by its recipe no longer waits for its roads at all.
- **One problem file in X-Plane's lit art no longer stops night lighting from being saved to disk** for the rest of the session.
- Night lighting at the 180° meridian (Fiji, the Aleutians) reads the area across the line, and a road overlay updated mid-session no longer mislabels night lighting saved to disk.
- With `run --debug`, a `Night lighting: summary` line every minute reports how night textures were served and how long they took.

**Dashboard**

- **The latency line describes the last five minutes**, not the whole session, so a slow cold start no longer keeps it red for the rest of the flight. When nothing waited in that time it reads `none waited in 5 min` in green; timeouts stay counted in grey as `(session)`.

**Logs**

- Panic reports from two threads at once are no longer mixed together in the flight log.

## What changed since 0.5.0

Everything under "What changed since beta.3" above, and:

**macOS**

- **No kernel extension.** XEarthLayer mounts through macFUSE's FSKit backend only. There is no Recovery step and no kernel extension approval, and the `fuse.macos_backend` setting is gone.
- **External drives.** At startup, XEarthLayer checks that the drive holding X-Plane honours ownership, and recreates its mount folder if it is empty, because FSKit refuses a folder made while ownership was off. A failed mount now names the likely causes rather than only macFUSE's `os error 35`.
- **Quitting leaves nothing mounted.** `q`, Ctrl+C and SIGTERM unmount the scenery, and a Ctrl+C during the first seconds of startup now does too (on Linux as well).
- **`xearthlayer diagnostics` has a macFUSE section**: the macFUSE version, whether its FSKit framework is present, and XEarthLayer's volume while it runs. The flight log records the same once after mounting.

**Scenery tiles**

- **No more magenta squares that stay.** An answer from the imagery server that is not an image, such as an error page, is retried and never saved, a tile with any unusable piece is shown but not kept, and bad pieces already in the cache are removed the first time they are used.
- **Tiles are built faster**: imagery is decoded straight into the form the tile needs, and each texture is encoded into one buffer of exactly its size.
- **A tile that finishes just as X-Plane stops waiting for it is kept**, and the first tile timeout no longer stalls other requests.

**Night lighting**

- **Roads light up at night.** Motorways and main roads carry chains of street lamps, read from the road overlays and airport packs X-Plane loads in your `scenery_packs.ini` order, X-World Pro included. An area with no road overlay has no road lights, as it has no roads in the simulator.
- **Close to the aircraft, X-Plane's lights take over.** The lit layer fades to a quarter of its light as you close in and then leaves the ground beneath you to X-Plane's 3D lights.
- **Cities are whiter.** Most neighbourhoods are now LED white, the remaining sodium districts a softer amber, and distant towns keep their light and colour instead of fading to orange.
- Night lighting saved on disk by 0.5.0 is generated again the first time it is needed, so the first night flight in each area does more work.

**Network**

- **`network.connections` (`max`, `high`, `low`)** sets how many connections XEarthLayer opens: for imagery X-Plane is waiting on, for prefetch, kept open to the imagery servers, and for package downloads. The default is `high`, which opens 80% of `max`; `low` opens 65%.

**Cache and configuration**

- **Each imagery provider keeps its own downloaded imagery**, so switching provider can no longer mix two providers' imagery in one tile.
- **`xearthlayer cache clear` deletes only the cache**, and refuses while `xearthlayer run` or a package operation is running. `xearthlayer cache stats` counts per provider and tier.
- **`xearthlayer run --no-cache` and `--no-prefetch` work.** Both only changed the startup message.
- **Settings outside their range are refused** when `config.ini` is read, and a `config.ini` that cannot be read is no longer replaced with defaults.

**Dashboard**

- The headless status line, the panic report and the telemetry summary count the tiles being generated right now. The count was always 0, and it now reads "running".
- The Prefetch pane's meter is labelled **Utilization** and has a twelve-second sparkline.
- On Linux, "Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified" no longer appears over the dashboard when the shell has a stale `DISPLAY`, and game overlays such as MangoHud no longer run inside XEarthLayer.

**Removed**

- **BC3 texture compression, `texture.format` and `run --dds-format`.** Choosing BC3 never produced usable scenery, only magenta placeholders.

## What we most want tested

### 1. Distant terrain

Run `xearthlayer cache clear` (or fly somewhere new), then fly by day over towns, hills or a coastline.

- Does distant terrain look right against terrain closer in? It should look lighter and more detailed than in beta.3, never washed out.
- Do you see a brightness step anywhere in the distance, along a line where X-Plane switches between two levels of a texture, or between neighbouring tiles?
- Screenshots help, with the location and, if you can, the same view in beta.3.

### 2. The GPU encoder

If you have a GPU that X-Plane does not render with (a second GPU, or the integrated GPU beside a dedicated one), try `xearthlayer config set texture.compressor gpu`:

- Do scene loads and boundary crossings feel as fast as with the default CPU encoder (ISPC), or faster?
- Does the Status pane ever say `GPU failed, encoding on CPU (ISPC)`? If so, send the flight log: the reason is in it.
- Send a few `GPU encode sample` lines from the flight log with your GPU model. They tell us how the GPU encoder does on hardware other than ours.

On a Mac, or a PC with one GPU, the GPU is the one X-Plane renders with, and XEarthLayer warns about that when you choose it. The default CPU encoder is the right choice there.

### 3. Night flights

- Do night textures appear as quickly as day scenery when an area loads, without dark patches that fill in later?
- Do areas lit only by roads (motorways between towns, with a road overlay installed) light up?
- If you can, fly one night leg with `xearthlayer run --debug` and send the `Night lighting: summary` lines.

### 4. Your normal flights

Fly your usual routes, by day and by night, and tell us about anything that would stop you recommending this build: pauses or purple tiles at DSF boundary crossings, slow starts, missing scenery, road lamps where there is no road, or SimHeaven X-World Pro misbehaving with `packages.xworld_pro` on. On a Mac, quit with `q`, with Ctrl+C, and once during startup; afterwards, `mount | grep zzXEL` should print nothing. If XEarthLayer ever made your router drop out, tell us your router model and which `network.connections` level stays stable.

## How to report

The flight log is `xearthlayer.log`, and the package manager's log is `xearthlayer-packages.log`, both at `~/.local/state/xearthlayer/` on Linux and in `~/Library/Logs/XEarthLayer/` on macOS unless you changed `logging.file`. `xearthlayer run` empties the flight log when it starts, so copy it before the next flight. Then run:

```bash
xearthlayer --version
xearthlayer diagnostics
```

The most useful report is your route, aircraft and flight time, the last few `Prefetch sample` lines from the flight log, and what looked wrong. For a GPU report, include your GPU and the `GPU encode sample` lines. For a network report, include your router or modem model, your connection speed, and the `Network connections` line near the top of the flight log.

**On macOS, if the mount fails**, macFUSE's own message (`os error 35`) rarely says why. The reason is in the system log; run this right after the failure and include its output:

```bash
/usr/bin/log show --last 5m --predicate 'process == "fskitd"'
```

---

## Known issues, please don't report these

**Distant levels of tiles cached before beta.4 are darker** than those of new tiles until the cache replaces them. `xearthlayer cache clear` rebuilds them all.

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Saving a setting rewrites `config.ini` from its template.** Comments you added to the file by hand are lost, as they are with `xearthlayer config set`. The values are kept.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**
